title: Chrysanthemum
subtitle: Hollow brass tubes stack into mountains beyond counting.

trails.title: Cloak and Statue
trails.description: In times of war, unreliable information spreads faster than truth, making it impossible to separate fact from fiction.

content.text:
"Have you heard about the 'Sentinel'? I saw her that night. Before anyone could react, old Noah was already down. The shot was unbelievable!"
"Did you get a clear look at her?"
"It was too dark to see much, just a figure wearing a cloak. But I'm almost certain she was carrying a Lebel rifle; she's probably on our side!"
"I wouldn't be so sure. They say she's the one that took out General Mathis two weeks ago. Might be someone playing both sides."
"Either way, having that warmonger gone is good for us all—ow! That hurts!"
"Bear with it, I'm almost finished."
Marsha soaks a towel in cold water and wrings it out. The wounded soldier's fever still hasn't broken. Her eyes move from one amputee to the next, checking each stump for signs of infection.
"Listen," another soldier cuts in, his face wrapped in bandages with only one eye visible. "The 'Sentinel' doesn't take sides because she isn't human. That's no rifle; it's a javelin or a spear. And she's got wings, silent as a bat. During the day, she turns into a stone statue. You could walk right past without noticing. But at night, she comes alive and hunts. Ever seen those church Gargoyles? That's exactly what she looks like."
"Maybe those wings were just her cloak," the first soldier insists.
"It's more than that. My comrade saw bullets hit her, but she didn't even flinch, like they were hitting a solid rock. Hey, Johnny, isn't that right? Johnny?"
Marsha pauses before looking up.
"Johnny died just after dawn this morning."

items.text: Chrysanthemum

"Since the first grenade exploded in our trench, 
we've been dreaming of the moment when the guns fall silent and our commander calls out 'The war is over.'"

"The marshals will attend the victory banquet in His Majesty's palace, 
the officers will pin shiny medals on their chests, and we will get to go home."

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: Out of my way, soldiers! I said make way!
His call to arms is passed through the winding trenches, passing over veterans slumped against the walls with indifference.

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: What's wrong?
Major Braun, the battalion commander, storms around a corner, followed by a long line of recruits with heads bowed.

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: Wilhelm, 2nd Company.

items.speaker: Wilhelm
items.text: Yes, Major.
Wilhelm straightens up, meeting the eyes of his commander.
Major Braun points to the line of recruits behind him, their faces blank and strangely foreign.

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: You'll be in charge of these runts from now on, and I'll need you to choose the pick of this litter to join the stormtroopers.

items.speaker: Wilhelm
items.text: Yes, Major.
The major claps Wilhelm on his shoulder and boldly steps up to a firing position.
He clears his throat.

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: Soldiers, I have some bad news.

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: Half an hour ago in Montpaix, at the site of this so-called parley, our representative, Colonel Hirschfelder, was assassinated by a French sniper.

items.speaker: Rudolph
items.text: Wh-What?
Helmets swivel, voices turn from sharp whispers to despair.

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: Nonsense! What the devil is he talking about?! How could a sniper have made it so far behind our lines!

items.speaker: Wilhelm
items.text: Shh!
The major stands above the murmurs.

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: Soldiers! We can't let our enemies sow fear within our ranks!

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: Let their desperate attack bring us together and give us the strength to destroy them once and for all! They will pay in blood for what they've done!
The mingling of voices churns into an ominous hum within the trench.

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: What the hell! I thought this was finally going to end.

items.speaker: Rudolph
items.text: I can't. I can't even force myself to care.

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: With hate and rage, they scheme to destroy our fatherland! But we march against them with the strength and cunning of wolves! Will you stand with me, soldiers? Will you stand for the Kaiser and for victory?!

items.speaker: Soldiers
items.text: Yes, Major!

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: Very good!

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: You've shown me your steel, soldiers! You are the pride of the fatherland!

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: Victory lies ahead, ready for the taking! Now, take up your rifle and get back to your positions!
With his impromptu speech over, he drops down from the firing platform and leads a further cadre down the line.
Second Company's new recruits tote bags so heavy they look liable to sink into the mud.
The company's vets close in to offer relief.

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: Hey, boy, what's that you're holding? You got a fresh tin? Verbena? Sausages?
Their questions slide off the recruits, slipping down through the cracks of the boards at their feet.
Some glance up from under oversized helmets, wide eyes locking with the tattered vets.

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: God! Did you see the way they looked at us? It was like there was nothing behind their eyes.

items.speaker: Rudolph
items.text: Erich, did you notice ... I don't think they understood a word you said.

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: Shameful.
Erich throws a hand in the air, shaking his head as he walks off.
But Wilhelm musters up his sense of obligation as company commander, patting a recruit's helmet enthusiastically.

items.speaker: Wilhelm
items.text: Come on, boys, follow me. I'll show you to your dugout.

items.speaker: Wilhelm
items.text: Mind the gaps on the duckboards.

items.speaker: Rudolph
items.text: Wil—er, Mr. Hauptmann, perhaps first we should drill them on keeping their heads down and avoiding artillery. Remember how many comrades we lost in our first days?

items.speaker: Wilhelm
items.text: Not now. First we need to ...

items.speaker: Wilhelm
items.text: Take cover!

items.speaker: Wilhelm
items.text: Get in there! Move!
Another body slumps to the ground. A shovel bites into the earth beside it.
The sound of artillery rumbles through the woods like a distant storm.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: It seems peace lies beyond our grasp.
He crouches and brushes aside some caked mud from a half-rotten arm.
He doesn't notice, or pays no heed to, the soft scrape of metal ascending up the hill.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Charon?
His hands go still. Then he rises.
He lingers wordlessly on the face that greets him.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: You don't remember who I am?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Your presence is familiar, but faces and names come slowly. There are so many memories here. It can be difficult to tell what is ... from what was.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: I'll wait a little longer next time.
Marsha turns her eyes to a stone monument placed at the base of the hill.
A slanted slab, laid flat on the ground, etched with elegant carvings.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: The Patriots? Did you make this cenotaph?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: A stranger brought it here. A gift for the dead.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: I see ...

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: I found your major's package. Here.
She hands the figure a thin envelope—along with it, a handwritten note.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: A message came for you, I think. From the front. It seems your major needs you to report back immediately.
Charon unfolds the note.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Yes. Soldiers must go where they are ordered.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Another thing. They're sending a new head of security to oversee the safe zone.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: His name is Creius, a tall man with red hair. He'll be responsible for investigating the assassination. You can contact him if you need anything.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: The Foundation has already tightened security on every road to the town. I don't think you'll run into ...

items.speaker: Marianne
items.text: She appears once again on a weed-choked dirt path.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: ... any danger on your way back.
Raincloak, rifle, that distinctive headpiece—Marsha could never mistake her.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: You're ...
Marsha steps forward, only to be blocked by the gravekeeper.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: The dead rest here. They have seen enough violence.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: You don't know what she did. She ...
A burst of breathy air rushes out behind clenched teeth. Though she tries to restrain herself, her hand climbs up to the sidearm at her waist.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Do you know her?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: She brought the cenotaph to honor the dead.
The stranger walks to the monument, standing perfectly still before it and paying no heed to either of them.
She pulls a single white wild chrysanthemum from her cloak.
Her stone-like skin stands out against the soft petals.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Her skin ... It looks as if it were made of stone. And that headwear, I feel I've seen it elsewhere.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Could you possibly be ...
Then a soft rumble, grumbling chanting. Even without hearing the words, she understands what it is: prayer.
The broken shell is abandoned, granting an end to endless penance.
May thy souls travel through the arches from darkness to peace.
May thy path be unfettered by eyes of red as you reach for paradise.
The white flower is left at the foot of the stone.
She pauses in thought, then traces a strange shape in the air.
The ritual is over. The mourner turns and meets Marsha's guarded eyes.
We meet again, young knight.
